subject: TPS & token-mix baseline — Dedicated vs VPC sizing follow-up for Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: TPS & token-mix baseline — Dedicated vs VPC sizing follow-up for Aurelia Health

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can size a dedicated pool and compare it to a private VPC option: 

Summary of what I heard on the call
- Primary need: inference for two clinical-assistant models (triage + summarization) with PHI handling; preference leaning toward Dedicated or Private VPC for data isolation and auditability.
- SLA/latency expectations: sub-300ms p95 on short queries; bursty daytime traffic with 2x peaks.
- Current hosting: internal staging on a small GPU fleet; production traffic forecast ~250–400 TPS for combined endpoints.

Questions needed for an accurate dedicated-sizing sketch (please fill or correct):
1) TPS targets: baseline steady-state target vs peak burst target (e.g., steady 250 TPS, peak 400 TPS)?
2) Token mix: typical prompt length and response length per model (avg prompt tokens / avg response tokens).
3) Concurrency expectations: average parallel requests vs max concurrent sessions during peaks.
4) Model variants: are both models running the same checkpoint/size (e.g., Llama-2-70B / opt-13B) or different families?
5) Any requirement for on-prem-only hardware (air-gapped) vs VPC-hosted dedicated pool?

I've attached a capacity workbook (aurelia_capacity_workbook.xlsx) — if you can drop the numbers into the "traffic & tokens" tab we will:
- produce a recommended GPU mix (H100 80GB vs A100 40GB count),
- map an expected TPS-to-GPU ratio given Redwood's batching/kv-cache assumptions, and
- provide committed-hour vs burstable pricing scenarios (see attached pricing PDF).

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the workbook and send it back (or I can hop on a 30-min call to walk through it)
- We return a sizing brief and cost delta for Dedicated vs Private VPC within 48 business hours of receiving the workbook
- If Dedicated looks right, schedule a short ops call with Karthik to review autoscale/fallback rules and audit log expectations

Happy to schedule the workbook walk-through tomorrow or Thursday — what times work for you?

Thanks,
--
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: aurelia_capacity_workbook.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf

From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@aureliahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TPS & token-mix baseline — Dedicated vs VPC sizing follow-up for Aurelia Health

Hi Priyom — thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. A few clarifications from our side: 

Traffic & tokens
- Steady-state target: ~300 TPS across both endpoints (combined).
- Peak/day: expected up to 450 TPS for short windows (15–30 min) during clinical shift changes.
- Model A (triage): avg prompt 90 tokens, avg response 220 tokens. Roughly 65% of traffic.
- Model B (summarization): avg prompt 160 tokens, avg response 600 tokens. Roughly 35% of traffic.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent requests 120–160, peaks up to ~320 concurrent.

Model details
- Both models are different sizes: triage is a 13B-family fine-tuned model; summarization is a 70B open model. We plan to run both in prod.

Deployment preferences
- Data isolation is mandatory (PHI). Private VPC is preferred if Dedicated in a shared cloud cannot guarantee our KMS/HSM key control. Procurement will evaluate both.

Procurement question
- Do you have a minimum committed capacity term for Dedicated? We typically negotiate quarterly commits.

Availability
- I can do a 30-min call Thursday 14:00–15:00 PST. Please include anyone who will speak to GPU mapping and SLA mechanics.

Sarah Lopez
Head of Applied ML | Aurelia Health
sarah.lopez@aureliahealth.com | +1 (617) 555-8888

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2026 12:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: TPS & token-mix baseline — sizing notes / internal

Priyom / Ben — quick internal note before we respond to Sarah: 

- Given the token mix (90/220 and 160/600) and the model families (13B + 70B), a conservative starting layout is: 1x H100 80GB for the 70B summarization model (to preserve perf and KV cache headroom) + 2–3x A100 80GB-equivalent slots for multiplexing the 13B triage model with high concurrency. If H100 is constrained, a 2x A100-80GB split with smarter routing could work but will raise latency on the 70B.
- Redwood's continuous-batching and KV cache typically raises effective throughput by ~1.8x for repeat contexts — we should explicitly state the cache hit assumptions in the sizing brief.
- For the peak concurrency (320), we'll recommend autoscale headroom for bursts plus a warm standby pool (burst capacity SLA).
- Ask procurement about committed-hours cadence: quarterly commits are reasonable; we should prepare a quarterly and annual pricing alternative.

I'll join the Thursday call; I'll draft a 1-page sizing note to attach to the workbook before we send.

Karthik
VP, Solution Architecture | Redwood Inference
